internal_mechanism_claims.text: The linked Yang--Mills procedures construct alternatives along three connected axes. A regulator atlas compares carriers, measures, boundary conditions, gauge invariance, locality, reflection positivity, and closure under blocking; it chooses a primary representation and an adversarial alternative by their missing theorem obligations. Observable-core construction asks whether the selected observables separate states and generate the physical sectors needed by a spectral argument, then seeks a hidden-sector countermodel. The representation calculus specifies observable pullbacks, state pushforwards, their compatibility, and observable-indexed approximation errors. It distinguishes equivalence from coarse-graining or a conjectural correspondence. Restricted-model calibration tests these proposals on massive, massless, finite-volume, and hidden-sector cases and revises definitions that produce false positives. This is the substantive frontier-building work compressed by the native projection: discovering which representation and observable choices expose a tractable missing implication, while preserving what could invalidate transfer.

A small intersection moment therefore cannot replace the history-uniform conditional ceiling required by the domination argument. The next proof task is to identify an exposure state and prove its normalized conditional bound, not to declare domination from that moment. This source-prescribed counterexample tests a proposed proof mechanism; it proves no Yang--Mills, continuum, or Hamiltonian-gap conclusion.

internal_mechanism_claims.text: The Yang--Mills proof bindings go substantially beyond packaging a conditional formula. Adaptive block domination fixes the exposure filtration and retained boundary information, bounds normalized probability on a good chart, and charges the complementary configurations through a multi-link estimate. Heat-kernel prefactors, chart mass, Haar Jacobians, overlap, and remainder oscillation enter the normalized comparison; a pointwise action estimate alone does not supply it. A state-weighted alternative proves a positive-kernel drift inequality $QV\leq q_VV$, controls the initial weight moment, and derives iteration before checking a strict cluster threshold. Retained-state sufficiency, positive-mass histories, and uniformity in volume and boundary conditions are independent obligations. Finite-block and enclosure candidates make parts of these burdens checkable; exact finite checks do not discharge full-measure, repeated-RG, continuum, or reconstruction hypotheses. The prescribed broader programme separates basin entry, controlled iteration, physical-unit decay, positivity, observable density, and continuum passage. These are implication dependencies to prove, not guaranteed successes or an execution order inferred from the skill list.

internal_mechanism_claims.text: The result-elaboration skills first recover the draft's smallest honest contribution and classify each expansion marker by its mathematical role. A missing coefficient, finite-object definition, transfer theorem, uniform estimate, and explanatory paragraph require different work. Open-module decomposition separates exact algebra or finite matrix checking from generative construction of estimates and proof strategies. The planner orders needs by genuine dependence: coefficients precede sign tests, and transfer certificates precede stronger application claims. Finite-object formalization specifies the carrier, indices, equivalence or support rule, quantitative measure, worked non-example, and the lemma that may consume the object. Proof-packet derivation then states each inference from its definitions and hypotheses, localizing a missing lemma or countermodel when it fails. Prior-art and disqualifier review test novelty and scope; narrative integration explains the result in the argument. Thus the four native occurrences compress an evidence-sensitive programme of mathematical elaboration, not a single generic request to expand prose.
